title: New State Prisons “Will Not Be Operated by Private Companies,” Sheinbaum Says
author: Anahí Del Ángel
content:
_This article by[Anahí Del Ángel](https://contralinea.com.mx/author/anahida/)
originally appeared in the [October 13, 2026 edition of
Contralínea](https://contralinea.com.mx/interno/semana/nuevos-penales-
estatales-no-van-a-ser-operados-por-privados-sheinbaum/), Mexico's leading
investigative journalism magazine._

The federal government will support six states of the Republic, **Sonora,
Sinaloa, Nayarit, the State of Mexico, Chiapas, and Veracruz** , in the
construction of a **prison** in each state to reduce **overcrowding** ,
announced President **Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo** , who assured that the new
facilities “will not be operated by **private companies**.”

During her morning press conference on October 13, the president explained
that the decision to provide economic resources to the state governments
responds to two reasons: respect for the **human rights** of persons deprived
of liberty and reasons of **security** , since overcrowding makes it difficult
to control prisons when the same number of guards is maintained.

She also linked the saturation of some prisons with the arrests carried out
during her administration, so she considered it necessary to expand the
infrastructure. The security report presented during the conference reported
**70,500 arrests** for high-impact crimes, from October 2024 to September
2026.

The head of the federal Executive emphasized that the new centers will have a
model oriented toward social reintegration and will be operated by the federal
**Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection (SSPC)** or by the state
Security Secretariats.

For his part, the Secretary of Security and Citizen Protection, Omar García
Harfuch, detailed the measures adopted in the area of prison security on the
president’s instructions.

In the case of Sinaloa, in light of the recent events at the **Mazatlán
Penitentiary Center** , he noted that Sheinbaum instructed that priority be
given to the construction of a new prison with federal resources. The complex
will have a projected capacity for **2,640 people** , modern infrastructure,
better surveillance systems, and the personnel necessary to strengthen its
operation and control.

While the project is carried out, the Mazatlán Penitentiary Center remains
reinforced with members of the National Guard and SSPC personnel assigned to
the Decentralized Administrative Body for Prevention and Social Readaptation.

Among the security actions, García Harfuch mentioned the strengthening of
**surveillance, supervision, and control** in federal social reintegration
centers to maintain order, **prevent criminal activities** , and improve
security conditions for both persons deprived of liberty and prison staff.

As he explained, from October 1, 2024 to September 30, 2026, **3,275 transfers
of persons deprived of liberty were carried out to reduce risks and strengthen
prison control** , in operations conducted by the decentralized administrative
body, in coordination with the National Guard.

He highlighted the carrying out of **nine operations in Sinaloa** , conducted
by personnel of the National Guard and the SSPC, through which 636 persons
deprived of liberty were transferred to various federal social reintegration
centers.

García Harfuch also reported that, in coordination with state authorities,
**614 transfers from local prisons** were carried out to address risk
situations and strengthen security.

In the same period, **10,513 ordinary inspections and 31 extraordinary
operations** were carried out, in which more than 306,000 prohibited objects
and substances were seized to prevent their use inside the prisons.

He added that emergency codes in federal prisons decreased by 35 percent
compared to the previous period, with a reduction in incidents related to
**fights, assaults, threats** , and other risk situations.

He also reported that the capabilities of the federal prison system were
strengthened with the addition of **1,192 new personnel** and the creation of
a prison reaction unit to address risk situations and support the states.

The official noted that this increase in personnel is part of the security
strategy promoted by President Claudia Sheinbaum since the beginning of her
administration. As part of the strengthening of other institutions, he
mentioned the **36 percent increase in the force strength of the National
Intelligence Center** and a 60 percent increase in the personnel of the
Financial Intelligence Unit.

In parallel, he indicated that the federal government is promoting
technological modernization and infrastructure improvement projects at the
Altiplano federal center and at federal prisons in Veracruz, Durango, and
Sinaloa.

In this context, he explained that work is underway on a new national prison
management model that contemplates, in addition to expanding infrastructure,
improving security protocols, professionalizing personnel, and modernizing
administration, surveillance, and control procedures.
